title: How a Ship Propeller Works in 60 Seconds 🚢🌀 #shorts
description:
A single aircraft carrier propeller can weigh around 33 tonnes. The engine spins a long shaft, and each twisted blade creates low pressure in front and high pressure behind, throwing water backward so the ship moves forward. Spin too fast and the water turns into vapor bubbles, called cavitation, which can eat away the metal. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#ship #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: One aircraft carrier propeller can weigh around *33 tonnes*. And it moves the whole ship.

steps.label: Shaft
steps.text: The ship's engine spins a long *shaft* that runs out through the back of the hull.

steps.label: Blades
steps.text: Each *blade* is twisted, like a slice of a screw, so it meets the water at an angle.

steps.label: Pressure
steps.text: As it spins, each blade makes *low pressure* in front and *high pressure* behind.

steps.label: Thrust
steps.text: That throws a jet of water backward, and the water pushes the ship *forward*.

steps.label: Cavitation
steps.text: Spin too fast, and the water turns into vapor bubbles. This *cavitation* can eat away the metal.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, twist, *push*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
